blocks.raw: <Tip>Testable anchor: At Manila's latitude (14.6°N), winter-solstice noon solar altitude is 59.5°, roughly 2.3× higher than New York (40°N) winter altitude of 26°. This single fact explains why Philippine design ignores "winter heating" entirely—winter sun is still intense. Philippine design problem is *summer cooling*, not winter warmth.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <Note>East-west orientation (windows facing E-W) creates equivleant solar gain on both sides throughout the year in Philippines latitude. North-south orientation (windows facing N-S) allows deep overhangs to control S-facing sun while N-facing facades remain naturally shaded. This is why "true cardinal orientation" performs better than random orientation—the ability to design asymmetrical shading strategies based on cardinal direction.</Note>

blocks.raw: <Warn>The most common error: applying temperate-zone logic that "south is good for heating." In Philippines, south-facing windows still require 3m+ overhangs even in winter (59.5° altitude requires tan(59.5°) = 1.6 m depth for 2m window height = 3.2m minimum). There is no free solar gain benefit in Philippines. Every facade requires aggressive shading. East-west elongation is not optional—it's mandatory.</Warn>
